q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a leather belt?
title: Leather belt carbon footprint per piece
short: Take the leather area per belt, including cutting waste, and multiply by your tannery's per-square-foot figure. Add the buckle by metal weight, edge paint, stitching and packing, then divide the unit's electricity by belts passed.
audience: Leather goods makers, including Kanpur and Chennai units

ul: Finished leather per belt from strap length and width, plus cutting waste.
Buckle and keeper: zinc alloy, brass or steel by weight.
Strap cutting, skiving, creasing and stitching machines.

p: Leather is usually most of the total, so the tannery's figure matters most. Report per belt by width and length.

example.title: Worked example: belt unit per piece (one month)
lines: Plant total: 5,680 / 25,000 = 0.227 kg CO2 per belt
Add leather and buckles for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
